speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset lower back pain that radiates down your leg. Can you describe exactly where the pain travels and if you have noticed any weakness, numbness, or tingling in that leg?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. To help narrow down the cause, can you tell me if the pain follows a specific path, such as down the back of the thigh and calf, or along the outer side of the leg? Also, have you noticed any specific movements that worsen the pain, like bending forward or coughing?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sharp lower back pain radiating to the leg and foot. I also have Pain worsens with movement, The onset of pain while exercising.

speaker: Doctor
text: The radiation down the side of the leg suggests involvement of the L5 nerve root. Do you have any difficulty lifting your foot or toes upwards (foot drop), and is the pain worsened by coughing, sneezing, or straining?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. No prior episodes of similar pain. Social history: Non-smoker, rarely drinks alcohol. Regular gym-goer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any numbness or tingling on the top of your foot or between your big and second toes? Additionally, does straightening your leg while lying down reproduce or worsen the pain in your back and leg?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, weight loss, changes in bowel or bladder function.

speaker: Doctor
text: It is reassuring that you have no red flag symptoms like bowel or bladder issues. I would like to perform a Straight Leg Raise test to see if it reproduces your leg pain, and I will also check your reflexes and strength in that leg.
